nutshell: Multi-target multi-camera (MTMC) tracking research has been bottlenecked by DukeMTMC's privacy-driven withdrawal and by existing alternatives being either synthetic or collected in small, controlled camera networks. MTMMC is a new large-scale real-world dataset - 16 spatially-aligned, temporally-synced RGB+thermal cameras across a campus and a factory, 3.6M frames, 3,669 consented identities - built as a superset test-bed for person detection, re-identification, single- and multi-camera tracking, plus two new multi-modal (RGB+thermal) learning setups.
contributions: A new large-scale real-world MTMC dataset: 16 multi-modal (RGB + thermal, spatially aligned and temporally synchronized) cameras across two environments (campus, factory), 25 scenarios, 3,052,800 frames, 3,669 person identities, collected with informed consent from 623 paid actors and de-identification (face blurring) of 107 incidental non-actors.

First MTMC dataset to include a thermal modality, enabling two new experimental setups introduced in this paper: modality fusion (input- and feature-level RGB+thermal fusion for tracking) and modality drop (train on RGB+thermal, deploy on RGB-only via knowledge distillation, multi-modal reconstruction, or multi-modal contrastive learning - motivated by real CCTV systems that are RGB-only).

Baseline results and reference scores across four subtasks - person detection (Faster RCNN, YOLOX), re-identification (AGW), single-camera MOT (JDE, QDTrack, CenterTrack, ByteTrack), and full MTMC (QDTrack + BoT with optimization-based vs. clustering-based multi-camera association) - including cross-dataset generalization experiments (e.g., pretraining on MTMMC transfers better to Market-1501/MOT17 than the alternatives compared) and a real+synthetic (MOTSynth) pretraining synergy result.
deficiencies: Every 'MTMMC improves generalization' claim (Re-ID: MTMMC-reID -> Market-1501 beats MSMT17 -> Market-1501; MOT: MTMMC -> MOT17 beats the reverse direction) rests on a single source/target dataset pair with no repeated runs or additional target datasets, so it's unclear whether the effect is really about MTMMC's diversity specifically, or just an artifact of that one comparison.

The paper frames MTMMC-reID's lower Rank-1/mAP (76.0/45.6 vs. Market-1501's 95.3/88.2 and MSMT17's 78.3/55.6, Table 3) as evidence of beneficial task 'difficulty' and 'complexity,' but never rules out the more mundane alternative that a semi-automatic annotation pipeline simply introduces more label noise than the fully manual Market-1501/MSMT17 pipelines - no controlled ablation separates genuine scene difficulty from annotation quality.

Table 4's MOT results report FP = 439,646 and FN = 439,646 as exactly identical values for QDTrack's combined-training row evaluated on MTMMC - an implausible coincidence that looks like a copy-paste error in the table, and it is neither flagged nor explained anywhere in the text.

As a dataset/benchmark paper making real-world-representativeness claims, there's no quantitative demographic breakdown (age/gender counts, only 'wide range' is stated) and no discussion of how the specific choice of two sites over two days in two seasons might bias which real-world tracking difficulties are actually represented.
notable: The paper explicitly recruited and paid actors who gave informed consent, separately from de-identifying 107 incidental bystanders (non-actors) - a more careful consent protocol than DukeMTMC's, and the paper frames this directly as filling the gap left by DukeMTMC's privacy-driven withdrawal (also referenced by name in the ReMix paper from the WACV2025 batch, which continued to use the withdrawn DukeMTMC despite the same concern - worth cross-referencing if this dataset review touches dataset ethics). Also notable: unlike the method papers elsewhere in this batch, this paper proposes no new re-identification model at all - it uses an off-the-shelf AGW model purely to characterize the dataset's difficulty, so its 'Re-ID contribution' is entirely about data, not algorithms.
